trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Specialist Solution Analyst
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: Work as part of a DevOps team, leverage specialist analysis & testing tools, frameworks, techniques and practices to elicit, define and organize business requirements. Translate & document business requirements into user stories & specifications (Full Stack, Cross System) detailing integration points, business & associated risk / opportunities to be realised. And following this analysis, work collaboratively within squads during design & delivery activity including assuming responsibility for manual application testing processes, frameworks & outcomes
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Proactively build relationships, apply analytical techniques to elicit and validate business (product & service) needs ahead of demand
  - Implement routines to get to know / become an expert in various business processes (e.g. spend time in business & with users)
  - Translate elicited needs and knowledge acquired into user story format that is immediately usable for DevOps teams (right languaging, format for building & testing)
  - Prepare and prioritise the backlog of requirements for the user stories linked to the proposed solutions
  - Work collaboratively with Tribe Leads (Technical Product / Service Owners) to build a roadmap & vision for the products and services (including detailed analysis requirements & solution scope)
  - Define measures of success & key outcomes for various solutions / changes including detailed acceptance criteria for all features
  - Define testing requirements (pass or fail test cases)
  - Support the development of detailed business cases (including defining solution characteristics, effort estimations etc.)
  - Translate business requirements into detailed systems requirements. Detailed system requirements must include all capabilities, interfaces and functionalities within and across technologies.
  - Build detailed user stories to be leveraged for system requirements design (modular)
  - Leverage business analysis & modeling tools and apply notation standards such as UML/BPMN to diagrammatically/visually document: business requirements, business processes, system processes & integration
  - Facilitate processes to ensure integrated requirements are socialized, understood & approved across the broad range of stakeholders to be impacted (this includes various processes e.g. risk / governance forums, change council, scrum meetings / DevOps team capability building, solution design sessions etc.)
  - Understand & leverage knowledge on the organisations technical landscape, environment and broader architecture to define integration points across tech stacks for various requirements
  - Work collaboratively with project / program teams, squads, scrum masters and engineers to define backlog, release & DevOps / project planning implications of the requirements development & roadmap (what should happen when)
  - Continuously improve system requirements mapping (e.g. leverage input from questions asked etc. to consistently improve the quality of the requirements analysis for easier interpretation by the development teams)
  - Work as part of the embedded DevOps team throughout the design process to review solution design (features and functionality)
  - Facilitate resolution during development & testing phases for any change requirements
  - Define the manual testing strategy & test cases for various solutions (where it makes sense to do so)
  - Define & validate quality & testing parameters (+/-) & plans for the solution (socialize & translate these to automation testing teams)
  - Develop manual testing frameworks and patterns for the solution
  - Lead the manual testing process for various solutions (e.g. execute test cases, analyse results)
  - Provide real time feedback to the DevOps teams on change requirements identified throughout the testing process
  - Review & monitor system stability, resilience etc. throughout the testing process (e.g. integration) & in production
  - Define & monitor overall backlog planning for effective solution delivery
  - Provide Developer & User support during user acceptance testing
  - Provide coaching & mentoring across the DevOps team as well as to developing analysts across the estate
  - Conduct peer reviews & problem solving within and across the broader team
Must-have requirements:
  - Bachelor's Degree: Information Technology
Location: Johannesburg
Team notes: DevOps team, working with Tribe Leads (Technical Product / Service Owners), scrum masters, engineers, and squads
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Absa Group

Johannesburg

About us
Empowering Africa's tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.

About the role
You will work inside a DevOps team, using specialist analysis and testing tools, frameworks and techniques to elicit, define and organise business requirements. You translate those requirements into full stack, cross system user stories and specifications that set out integration points, business value and associated risks. You then stay with the squad through design and delivery, and you own the manual testing process and its outcomes.

Your team
You work as part of an embedded DevOps team, alongside Tribe Leads (Technical Product / Service Owners), scrum masters, engineers and squads.

What you'll do
• Build relationships across the business and apply analytical techniques to elicit and validate product and service needs ahead of demand
• Spend time in the business and with users so you become an expert in the business processes you support
• Translate what you learn into user stories written in the language and format DevOps teams can build and test from
• Prepare and prioritise the backlog of requirements linked to proposed solutions
• Work with Tribe Leads (Technical Product / Service Owners) to build a roadmap and vision, including detailed analysis requirements and solution scope
• Define measures of success, key outcomes and detailed acceptance criteria for all features
• Translate business requirements into detailed system requirements covering all capabilities, interfaces and functionality within and across technologies
• Document business requirements, business processes, system processes and integration visually using modelling tools and notation standards such as UML and BPMN
• Use your knowledge of the technical landscape and broader architecture to define integration points across tech stacks
• Facilitate socialisation and approval of integrated requirements through risk and governance forums, change council, scrum meetings and solution design sessions
• Work with project and programme teams, squads, scrum masters and engineers to define backlog, release and delivery planning implications
• Support development of detailed business cases, including solution characteristics and effort estimations
• Define the manual testing strategy, test cases and pass or fail criteria, and develop manual testing frameworks and patterns
• Lead manual testing: execute test cases, analyse results and give the DevOps team real time feedback on change requirements
• Define and validate quality and testing parameters and plans, and translate these to automation testing teams
• Review and monitor system stability and resilience through testing and in production
• Support developers and users during user acceptance testing
• Coach and mentor people across the DevOps team and developing analysts across the estate, and conduct peer reviews and problem solving

What you need
• Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
